title: SMTO-BOOT-0014 — The model launcher can't use the two graphics cards selected
summary: This launcher splits the model across two different graphics cards (GPUs). The cards it was told to use aren't two different ones, or one isn't visible on this computer, so it stopped before loading the model.

html:
SMTO-BOOT-0014 — The model launcher can't use the two graphics cards selected

GUID: a2ad4f81-fd1a-4ce5-9223-d9924c084c7d
Slug: boot-gpu-selection-invalid
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • This launcher splits the model across two different graphics cards (GPUs). The cards it was told to use aren't two different ones, or one isn't visible on this computer, so it stopped before loading the model.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open a terminal and run nvidia-smi. Note the number shown for each graphics card and how much memory each one has. The launcher can only use cards the computer can see, and it expects the card with more memory to come first.
  2. Set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to those two card numbers, larger card first (for example 0,1). If you set LLAMA_DEVICES yourself, set it to CUDA0,CUDA1 or remove it. CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES picks the physical cards; LLAMA_DEVICES must then name two different cards, CUDA0 and CUDA1, in that same order.
  3. Start the launcher again. To check the card names first without loading anything, add --dry-run; it only prints the command it would run. A dry run catches a mistyped or repeated card name in seconds, without downloading the large model file.
  4. If it still stops on a normal start, run CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 llama-server --list-devices (use your two card numbers) and check that CUDA0 and CUDA1 both appear. The launcher looks for both names in this list using those card numbers; a missing name means the model program can't see that card.

What success looks like

  • The launcher prints its list of graphics devices and then starts loading the model instead of stopping with this message.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full terminal output, including the SMTO-BOOT-0014 line and the Error reference line, plus the output of nvidia-smi, and send it to the person who manages this computer's model setup. Remove any passwords or tokens first. Don't keep restarting with the same card setting; it will stop the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The dual-GPU llama.cpp launcher stopped because LLAMA_DEVICES is not two distinct CUDA device names (such as CUDA0,CUDA1), or llama-server --list-devices does not list one of the selected devices under the current CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES.

What this means

  • Dual-device launcher parsing rejects anything other than two distinct CUDA IDs, or advertised device discovery lacks one of those IDs. The dual-device launcher stops before model launch. It checks selection syntax and, outside dry-run, the server's advertised devices. Two advertised devices do not establish their memory capacity, free memory or the success of the planned layer placement.

Why this can happen

  • Dual-device launcher parsing rejects anything other than two distinct CUDA IDs, or advertised device discovery lacks one of those IDs.

How to diagnose it

  • Check both IDs, their advertised availability and intended order; this error is not a GPU-memory test.

How to fix it

  • Set LLAMA_DEVICES to two distinct llama.cpp device names (default CUDA0,CUDA1) and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to the intended physical GPUs, larger first (default 0,1 with CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID). Confirm both names appear in llama-server --list-devices (DRY_RUN only checks the syntax); passing this check does not prove free memory or that the TENSOR_SPLIT/N_GPU_LAYERS placement fits.
  • Set LLAMA_DEVICES to the intended two CUDA device IDs with the larger GPU first.

Retry and execution caution

  • Choose two distinct advertised CUDA device IDs in the intended visible order before launching again.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact supported two-device selection validates with the intended larger GPU first.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The dual-device launcher stops before model launch. It checks selection syntax and, outside dry-run, the server's advertised devices.
  • Two advertised devices do not establish their memory capacity, free memory or the success of the planned layer placement.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
